Put another way, if the truth‑conditions of the left fragment cannot be evaluated without material that follows (because the main assertion, negation, scope‑reversal, or essential qualification appears later), assume the remainder will likely change or qualify the meaning and penalize the cut accordingly.

Cohesion (additional rule): strongly penalize cuts that split a single noun phrase (determiner/quantifier + head noun + essential post‑nominal modifiers) or that separate a verb from its core object or phrasal particle. When essential modifiers, relative/PP complements, numerals/quantifiers, or particles attach to a head on the other side of the cut, reduce cohesion sharply — such splits commonly produce lost references, detached modifiers, or wrong attachments in independent translations and should be avoided unless the remainder clearly neutralizes the dependency.
